Independent recomputations with my own script (own csv reader, own tokenizer, own confusion matrix, no import of qualdialect/qualreal): pooled row count 63,550 and per-language negative counts by awk over the raw tsv files (hau 7226/22152, ibo 4013/15715, pcm 6380/10556, yor 3296/15127); test-split shares 0.3257/0.2542/0.6027/0.2194 and lexicon-en sensitivity 0.009/0.022/0.090/0.004, specificity 0.995/0.996/0.954/0.999 and true hau-yor gap +0.1063 all match E1/E2; an analytic PPI-vs-human width ratio from the E1 confusion rates (Var(Y-f)+n/N Var(f) over Var(Y)) predicts 1.304 for nb-english on Pidgin at 400 items, observed 1.295. The computations are right; the prose ranges that summarise them are not (see claims).

Four mutants via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: NB likelihood denominator n[0]+2 -> n[1]+2 SURVIVED; match_rate off-by-one CAUGHT; dropping set() so token counts replace presence SURVIVED; prior term -> 0 SURVIVED (an equivalent mutant, since match_rate re-thresholds). experiments/run.py (the coverage/width/gap loop that produces every headline number) has no test at all; the only check on the estimator path is ppi_fast vs q.ppi on 10 items.
evidence.craft: Read qualdialect.py (93 lines), experiments/run.py (110), figure.py (38), test_qualdialect.py (49). Small, stdlib, seeded, deterministic, commits no tweet text. Defects: NB docstring says 'multinomial' but the model is presence-only with (n+2) Bernoulli smoothing and no absence terms (qualdialect.py:49); run.py docstring says 'a few minutes' (measured 6 s); cross-project imports by sys.path.insert into ../qual-real and ../qual-correction make the project fragile to edits there; one blank-line style slip in tests.
evidence.claims: Checked against results.txt with scratchpad/qual-dialect/tools/claims.py and by hand. Backed: true/coded gaps (+10.6 vs -6.5; +29.3 vs +7.1), naive coverage 0 everywhere, PPI gap coverage 93-96% at 400 (observed 0.930-0.962) and 91.8-96.6% over every target/size, PPI wider in all 54 gap rows, specificities 0.73-1.00, README E3 table rounding. Not backed: the bolded headline says word-list sensitivity 0.4-2.4% (file: 0.4-2.2% on hau/ibo/yor) and English-classifier sensitivity 0.4-10.8% (file: 1.9-10.8%); 'PPI 0.4-26% wider' (file: 0.3-26.4%). Limitations section is honest (no LLM, confounding, pooled sampling).
evidence.fitness: A researcher can plug any code(text)->0/1 into run.py and reproduce in seconds, which is useful. But the core finding (an English word list and an English-only NB do not read Hausa, Igbo, Yoruba) is near-tautological, and nearest prior work is uncited: PPI++ power tuning (Angelopoulos, Duchi, Zrnic 2023), which by construction is never asymptotically wider than human-only and would remove finding 4's 'never narrower'; design-based supervised learning (Egami et al. NeurIPS 2023); stratified PPI (Fisch et al. 2024) for the stratified audit it proposes; misclassification bias in automated content analysis (TeBlunthuis, Hase, Chan 2024); AfriSenti (Muhammad et al. 2023) with multilingual-model baselines. Novelty is not overstated in words, but the contribution beyond qual-correction is small.
evidence.domain: Against current practice for measuring differential coder error across groups: (1) vanilla PPI only, no power-tuned PPI++ or DSL, so 'PPI does not pay' is an artefact of the estimator choice; (2) no competent multilingual baseline (e.g. AfroXLMR/mBERT fine-tuned, the NaijaSenti paper's own baselines), so the coders are strawmen and say little about any realistic automated coder; (3) a single seeded train/test split, so nb-in-language results have no split variability; (4) 1,080 of 44,485 test tweets have exact-text duplicates in the training slice (2,415 duplicate rows corpus-wide), a leakage the README does not mention; (5) sensitivities and gaps reported without intervals. PPI formula itself matches Angelopoulos et al. 2023 (checked against qualml.ppi and analytically).

verdict: The pipeline is honest and reproducible: a fresh download and re-run gives a bit-identical results.txt in about 6 s, and independent recomputations of the row count, per-language shares, lexicon sensitivity/specificity, the true gaps and the PPI width ratio all match. What falls short of a senior measurement-error researcher's bar is the design and its write-up: the bolded headline misstates two sensitivity ranges, the 'PPI never narrower' finding is an artefact of using vanilla PPI with PPI++/DSL uncited, the coders are strawmen with no multilingual baseline, there is a small undisclosed train/test duplicate leak, and the code that produces the headline numbers is untested (3 of 4 seeded mutants survive, one equivalent). Correct, finished, not yet publishable.
